doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: George Guesnon and McNeil's first carnival job
summary: McNeil recalls banjoist George Guesnon and his first carnival truck job.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Oh. But this fellow, I know you know him. He plays a guitar player. He worked at the quarters sometimes. He plays, he's still one of the banjo players. George, his name is George something. Kind of heavy built up brown skin fellow with a sort of large hair. And he plays the- Oh, Lawrence Marrero. No, his name is George. George Gano. I don't know his last name. Pre-old George. Pre-old George. Yeah. With those Bush-Countdowns, the government all the way across. Yeah. I played one of my first carnival jobs with him. We played two jobs on a carnival day. And the first experience I had to play on, during the carnival, on the trucks, like they have the Elks crew, you know. And that was quite an experience too. His favorite nom is, uh, Some of These Days. And we had quite a time. That's a good old nommer though. He plays, right? He's a good guitar, banjo. He's an old nommer, been a lot of new ones. I think he still sticks to the banjo too. Yeah. He's teaching guitar and banjo mostly now. Oh yeah. I saw him-

Well, he plays trumpet too? A few weeks ago, but I was close enough to speak to him. He's on the banjo. Yeah. He's still using banjo in some of them bands and them over there. It sounds good too. He tried to get rid of bass, violin, and the tramo, and bring it back. And Clonett too, he brought all that back.

My first experience of knowing that I was really hitting it, you know. I played with guys like him. That was my first experience of playing with somebody the whole time. Been playing with most of the guys.
